summary: Multi-agent frameworks already support a planner or supervisor that delegates to separately configured workers. Implementing the pattern requires distinct model assignments plus explicit artifacts and checks; role labels alone do not create a reliable companion-model boundary.

items.text: LangChain subagents use a central supervisor that invokes isolated subagents as tools and controls the context passed into and returned from each call; each subagent can be configured with its own model and bounded tool set.

CrewAI's hierarchical process assigns a manager agent or manager model to plan, delegate, and validate work performed by specialist agents, providing a direct planner-reviewer versus executor structure.

Microsoft AutoGen SelectorGroupChat selects the next specialist through a model-based selector and permits agents with distinct model clients, tools, and descriptions; a planning agent can therefore route bounded tasks to cheaper executors.

Google Agent Development Kit composes agents through explicit sub-agent hierarchies and workflow agents for sequential, parallel, or loop execution; individual LLM agents can use separate model configurations.

RouteLLM provides learned routers and evaluation code for selecting between stronger and weaker models from preference data, useful for calibrating when a low-cost companion is sufficient rather than fixing the split by intuition.
